kept.title: Default escalation triggers: all five ON
kept.summary: ESCALATION_DEFAULTS() returns { ambiguous_intent, irreversible_action, low_confidence_high_impact, repeated_failure, scope_expansion } all true. These are the exact conditions that route a decision to a human; tunable per-workspace via POST /config { escalation }.

kept.title: Optimize-loop knobs: epsilon 0.01, diminishing_rounds 3
kept.summary: lib/optimize.js DEFAULTS = { epsilon: 0.01, diminishing_rounds: 3 } drive the converged-vs-iterate control. A negative/NaN override silently falls back to the default so a mis-set knob can't disable the control.

kept.title: Duplicate-detection threshold is 0.6; autowire is 0.25
kept.summary: SUGGEST_DUP_THRESHOLD=0.6 flags a new task as a likely re-plan duplicate of an OPEN non-note task. DEFAULT_AUTOWIRE_THRESHOLD=0.25 is the lower bar at which a seen task auto-gets a weighted context edge to each match. Two different cutoffs for two different jobs.

kept.title: MCP protocol version pinned to 2025-06-18
kept.summary: lib/mcp-core.js DEFAULT_PROTOCOL='2025-06-18' is echoed in the initialize response unless the client supplies its own protocolVersion. Shared by both transports (stdio mcp-graph.js and the daemon HTTP /mcp).

kept.title: Measure commands hard-capped at 120s
kept.summary: lib/measure.js DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 bounds any inline-metric measure command (execSync timeout) so a runaway command can't hang the daemon.

kept.title: Context edges default to weight 0.5; absent weight is back-compat
kept.summary: lib/overlay.js DEFAULT_CONTEXT_WEIGHT=0.5. An edge with no weight field reads back as 0.5, so old overlays load unchanged. Weight is ignored entirely for blocking/supersede edges — only context edges carry relevance weight.

kept.title: Auto-decision dedup threshold 0.45 (env-overridable)
kept.summary: scripts/extract-decisions.js DEDUP_THRESHOLD = EXTRACT_DEDUP_THRESHOLD env or 0.45; a proposed note scoring >= this against existing notes is dropped as already-known.

kept.title: Heartbeat-loop hard caps: 100k tokens, 200 iters, poll 30-1200s, batch 8
kept.summary: A fresh loop's config defaults are tokenBudget=100000, maxIterations=200, minPoll=30, maxPoll=1200, estPerTick=800, batch=8. These bound autonomous token burn; exceeding tokenBudget stops the loop with reason 'token budget exhausted'.

kept.title: Per-path worktree lease: O_EXCL 'wx', stale after dead-pid + 1h
kept.summary: lib/git.js guards each worktree path with a <wt>.lease sidecar written with flag 'wx' (O_EXCL) so the first writer wins; a second racer gets {contended,held}. A lease is reclaimable only when its owner pid is dead AND aged past ORCH_LEASE_STALE_MS (default 3600000ms / 1h). Re-entrant for the same pid.

kept.title: ORCH_WORKSPACE overrides cwd as the workspace pointer
kept.summary: mcp-graph.js uses ORCH_WORKSPACE || process.cwd() as the workspace it posts to the daemon. Without this env, a headless agent running inside a git worktree would hijack the global workspace pointer (Dogfood-finding #1) — repointing the live graph and blinding the agent to real learnings.

kept.title: Native task IDs are session-local; cross-session refs must be namespaced
kept.summary: Native Claude Code task IDs ('1','2',...) are unique only within a session. lib/native-tasks.js unions sessions into keys of the form '{session}/{id}', and intra-session blockedBy deps are namespaced to the same session. Any cross-session reference MUST be {session-uuid}/{id} — native IDs cannot hold this.

kept.title: Edit gate: default-ON, fail-OPEN, orchestrator source NOT exempt
kept.summary: hooks/orch-gate.sh denies Write/Edit (exit 2) unless the session holds an in_progress claim. It is active by default, opted out per-conversation via sessions/<id>.off or ORCH_GATE_OFF=1, and fails OPEN if the daemon is unreachable (never bricks editing). A path allowlist exempts memory/settings/CLAUDE.md/tmp, but the orchestrator's own source (~/.claude/orchestrator/**) is deliberately NOT exempted — that's the substantive work the gate exists to route.

kept.title: Bearer-token auth is off when no token configured; only write paths protected
kept.summary: daemon.js TOKEN = mcpCore.readToken(); null means auth OFF (localhost dev, back-compat). When set, /mcp + destructive/write endpoints (and any ?workspace= request) require the token via Authorization: Bearer, x-orch-token header, or ?token= query — so a connector URL can carry it.

kept.title: JSON responses send Connection: close to avoid request-splitting
kept.summary: daemon.js sends 'Connection: close' on JSON/HTML responses to avoid keep-alive request-splitting; only the SSE endpoints (/events) use keep-alive event-stream.

kept.title: embed() never throws — returns null and the daemon falls back to lexical
kept.summary: lib/embed.js wraps transformers.js + all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (ONNX, 384-dim, local, no hosted API/vector DB). Its contract: embed(text) returns 384 floats or null on ANY failure and NEVER throws; null is a first-class expected outcome (module missing, weights can't download) and callers fall back to lexical scoring. ESM-only lib reached via dynamic import() from this CommonJS module; model cache pinned under the daemon data dir (not node_modules).

kept.title: native-tasks.js is the SOLE adapter for an undocumented on-disk layout
kept.summary: The ~/.claude/tasks/{session}/{id}.json layout and projects-dir encoding are UNDOCUMENTED/internal Claude Code formats. lib/native-tasks.js is intentionally the single adapter — if a Claude Code version changes the format, only this file should need updating. Same caution applies to per-agent token figures read from transcript JSONL (daemon.js).

kept.title: Benchmark verdict: ON vs OFF work is parity; the cost is cache_read
kept.summary: The orch-ON vs orch-OFF study found actual work (output_tokens) is ~parity with/without the graph; the ENTIRE cost delta is cache_read of the loaded context. Compact get_learnings (~1-3k) vs full (~25k) moved cost-weighted gross from v2 1.63x to v3 1.03x (parity). Measure work with output_tokens, NOT 'gross - plumbing' net — MCP attribution is sticky and buckets cache_read into plumbing, producing a spurious savings figure.

kept.title: decideOptimize precedence: target then stuck then diminishing then budget then iterate
kept.summary: lib/optimize.js resolves first-match: target-converged FIRST (explicit target met beats all); STUCK before the silent stops so a problem failing every round escalates to a HUMAN rather than being quietly dropped; then diminishing-returns, then budget; else iterate with a DIFFERENT change. The only human-in-loop output is 'escalate' — never an auto-cancel/replan.

kept.title: Note nodes are bitemporal: supersede stamps validTo, never deletes
kept.summary: Note nodes carry validFrom/validTo + supersedes/supersededBy chains. Superseding an old note stamps its validTo (= the new note's validFrom) and links both directions WITHOUT deleting the row, so /search?asOf=T returns the fact CURRENT at T. validFrom defaults to creation but may be backdated; asOf (valid time) composes with knownAsOf (transaction time) for a bitemporal query.

kept.title: Autonomous loop HOLDS code work — never merges to main mid-run
kept.summary: Under the heartbeat loop, code-producing spawns work in an isolated orch/attempt/<slug> worktree off the CODE repo, commit there, and complete as 'MERGE PENDING' — never editing the live checkout, never merging to main, never calling request_guidance (which would halt the loop). Merges/conflicts/failures are all queued for the morning human review via the verdict + the pause/warn summary.

kept.title: Planner may only ADD nodes — touching in-flight work caused a runaway
kept.summary: self-learn-planner must NEVER cancel/supersede an in-flight task (in_progress/ready/not_ready — the 'no-fly zone') and never duplicate an open task; it only ADDs nodes (cap 1-3 initiatives). The guardrails header explicitly notes 'this skill caused a runaway once'. Re-planning live work is the user's call.

kept.title: Worktree GC is conservative: dry-run default, 24h retention, merged-only
kept.summary: scripts/gc-worktrees.js is DRY RUN by default (--confirm to execute), --retention-hours default 24. It removes only EMPTY dirs and GC-ELIGIBLE worktrees (clean AND fully merged into main AND unclaimed AND outside retention). A worktree with uncommitted changes OR unmerged commits is NEEDS-ATTENTION and never reaped — policy: durable value = merged code + recorded verdict, worktrees are ephemeral.

kept.title: Inline-UI connector needs mkcert HTTPS; mkcert -install needs a password
kept.summary: The daemon must be served over locally-trusted HTTPS to be added as a custom MCP connector (inline Apps UI). setup uses mkcert; cert generation is password-free but `mkcert -install` (local CA) triggers a macOS Keychain password — the setup skill must NEVER auto-run a password step, it asks the user to run it themselves.

kept.title: Token attribution: unparseable claim-window bound WIDENS the window
kept.summary: Per-task token totals prefer the assignee agent's own transcript; with no assignee the daemon falls back to a time-window correlation against the run. An unparseable/missing window bound widens the window (missing start -> -Infinity, missing end -> Date.now()) rather than failing the lookup — bias toward recovering a figure over dropping it.

kept.title: digestRejected feeds the planner a flat losing-approaches ledger
kept.summary: daemon.js digestRejected(verdicts, failures, labelFor) returns a rejected[] ledger so the planner scans losers in one pass: verdict losers as {approach, reason, beatenBy, source:'verdict'}, and genuine dead-end failures as {approach, reason, source:'failure'} — EXCLUDING superseded/duplicate/consolidated work. Exposed via /learnings so dependents avoid relitigating a settled loss.
